metadata.title: (In)Efficient Market States and Rough Volatility Detected via Grünwald-Letnikov Fractional Derivative

research_scenario.description: The study focuses on testing self-similarity in fractional processes under long-range dependence, particularly in financial applications such as realized volatility and equity index prices.

economic_mechanism.description: The paper introduces a regime-adaptive KS/GL–KS framework based on the discrete Grünwald–Letnikov (GL) fractional derivative to remove low-frequency long-memory singularity while preserving finite-dimensional H-self-similarity.
source_locators: <!-- page: 2 --> Section 2 Preliminaries and problem statement

variables.meaning: Fractional Brownian motion at time t with Hurst exponent H

data_processing.description: The paper uses crossed fractional Gaussian noises and applies the GL filter to transform the data into a short-memory regime for analysis.
source_locators: <!-- page: 4 --> Section 2.1 Problem Statement and the Long-Memory Issue

testing_methods.description: The study employs a Kolmogorov-Smirnov type statistic to compare empirical distribution functions of rescaled increments.
source_locators: <!-- page: 5 --> Section 2.1 Problem Statement and the Long-Memory Issue

robustness_and_failures.description: The paper discusses the phase transition in the asymptotic behavior of the KS statistic at H = 1/2 and the slow convergence rates in the long-memory regime.

tradability.description: The method is applied to financial time series to detect rough volatility and market efficiency states, suggesting practical applicability in trading strategies.

adaptation.project_fit: The GL-KS framework is highly relevant for high-frequency trading as it provides a robust method to detect market inefficiencies and rough volatility, which are critical for intraday strategies.
adaptation.adjustments_needed: The method needs to be adapted to use only historical data within the trading day, ensuring no look-ahead bias. The GL filter parameters may need optimization for high-frequency data.

extensions.hypothesis: A new feature based on the GL-filtered Hurst exponent could be developed to predict short-term mean reversion or momentum in intraday futures prices.
extensions.rationale: The GL-KS method effectively identifies persistent and anti-persistent market states, which can be leveraged to design trading signals.

extensions.hypothesis: The GL filter could be applied to volatility surfaces to detect rough volatility regimes in real-time, enhancing option pricing models.
extensions.rationale: The paper demonstrates the GL filter's effectiveness in neutralizing long-memory effects, making it suitable for real-time volatility estimation.
